blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present. Coupling a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders. Trained on human video and robot trajectories, $Z$-sight achieves 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points over the strongest baseline) and 73.3% across six Unitree G1 tasks (+20.0 points) at 110 ms per chunk, while remaining competitive on tabletop benchmarks.

We introduce 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight, a unified model that brings joint future-and-action
generation into the policy’s co-evolving native visual space
(Figure 1 ). A VLM encodes observations into spatial visual
tokens. By supervising future predictions against an exponential-moving-average
(EMA) teacher of this same vision encoder, perception and prediction remain
aligned throughout pre-training and downstream adaptation, without introducing
a video generator or an external target encoder.

blocks.en: 2  Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Vision-language-action models. Vision-language-action (VLA) models adapt pre-trained VLMs to output discrete
action tokens ( Zitkovich et al., 2023 ; Kim et al., 2025 ; Black et al., 2025b ; Pertsch et al., 2025 ) or continuous
actions via flow-matching experts ( Black et al., 2025a ; Bjorck et al., 2025 ; Wei et al., 2026a ) . Leveraging internet-scale
multimodal pre-training, these policies exhibit strong semantic reasoning and
instruction following. To preserve pre-trained representations while learning
continuous control, Driess et al. (2025) employ knowledge insulation, training
the VLM with discrete action tokens while a flow expert learns continuous
actions from detached VLM features. While effective at mapping current context
to actions, standard VLAs rely primarily on action labels, providing a
relatively sparse supervision signal. 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight builds upon this foundation and
augments it with generative latent world modeling.

blocks.en:
World action models and unified models. World action models (WAMs) capture physical dynamics by predicting future video
alongside actions, either jointly denoising video and actions on video
diffusion backbones ( Ye et al., 2026 ; Zhou et al., 2026 ) or using video
co-training while skipping test-time generation ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) . Motivated by this complementarity,
unified models combine a VLM with visual generation and action experts. For
example, Motus ( Bi et al., 2026 ) couples a VLM, a video generation expert, and an
action expert, while BagelVLA ( Hu et al., 2026 ) interleaves textual plans,
generated keyframes, and actions with single-step guidance. Related designs
include UP-VLA ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) , dual-stream VLAs ( Won et al., 2026 ) ,
F1 ( Lv et al., 2025 ) , InternVLA-A1 ( Cai et al., 2026a ) , and
MotuBrain ( Xiang et al., 2026 ) . However, relying on pixel or codec generation introduces
substantial computational cost. 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight instead performs joint
future-and-action generation directly in the VLM’s visual token space without a
video generator.

Latent world modeling and predictive policies. Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn representations by predicting
features rather than pixels ( Baevski et al., 2022 ; Assran et al., 2023 ; Bardes et al., 2024 ) against EMA teachers ( Grill et al., 2020 ) , enabling planning
with pre-trained visual features ( Zhou et al., 2025 ; Assran et al., 2025 ) . In
robotic control ( Lyu et al., 2026 ; Nilaksh et al., 2026 ) , implicit alignment
methods align internal policy activations with compact future
embeddings ( Zheng et al., 2025 ; NVIDIA, 2025 ) or spatial and world-model
features ( Li et al., 2026 ; Dao et al., 2026 ) without
generating a spatial future stream. Explicit latent predictors instead
supervise world tokens with frozen external teachers in
DreamVLA ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) , or frozen V-JEPA 2 and SigLIP encoders in
VLA-JEPA ( Sun et al., 2026 ) and UniJEPA ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) . Instead, 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight models future states as dense spatial tokens in the co-evolving perceptual
space of the policy’s own vision encoder, jointly denoising future tokens and
continuous actions via flow matching (Appendix G ).

blocks.en: 4  Experiments

blocks.en:
𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight jointly denoises future visual tokens and continuous actions within the
VLM’s native feature space. Our experiments evaluate the practical
benefits and underlying mechanisms of this design.
Specifically, we aim to answer four key questions.
(1) How does 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight perform compared to strong VLAs and video-based WAMs?
(Section 4.2 )
(2) How much do continued future supervision and the co-evolving native target
design contribute relative to implicit alignment and frozen external encoders?
(Section 4.3 )
(3) What scene changes does the foresight stream capture, and how does the
action expert rely on its content and uncertainty during execution?
(Section 4.4 )
(4) Can 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight retain online foresight at high efficiency?
(Section 4.5 )

设计的益处和基本机制。
具体而言,我们的目标是回答四个关键问题。
(1) Z\ mathcal{Z} - 相对于强VLA和基于视频的WAM,视觉表现如何?
(第4.2节)
(2)今后继续监管和共同发展本土目标需要多少?

(第4.3节)

stream with another episode’s valid prediction ( Swap ) preserves token

blocks.en: 5  Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight, a unified vision-language-action and latent world model.
By jointly denoising future spatial tokens and continuous actions in the VLM’s
co-evolving perceptual space, 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight unifies semantic reasoning, physical
foresight, and control without video generators or external encoders. Across
simulation and real-world humanoid tasks, 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight substantially improves
whole-body loco-manipulation over VLA and WAM baselines at high efficiency, and
controlled interventions confirm that the policy actively relies on its
predicted dynamics. More broadly, our findings show that a VLM’s perceptual
representations, when adapted jointly with foresight and control, provide an
effective substrate for embodied world modeling.

default head-mounted Intel RealSense D435i provides a narrow field of view
suited to tabletop tasks ( Dog and Puffs ), whereas tasks

blocks.en:
Rather than outputting raw whole-body joint targets, high-level policies act
through SONIC ( Luo et al., 2026 ) , a learned whole-body motion-tracking controller.
Each 78-D action comprises a latent SONIC motion token paired with joint
targets for both dexterous hands, while the 43-D proprioceptive state comprises
body joint positions and commanded hand targets. Demonstrations are collected
through the identical control interface by a teleoperator wearing a VR headset
whose tracked upper-body poses, hand commands, and locomotion inputs drive
SONIC at 50 Hz, recording synchronized camera frames, proprioception, motion
tokens, and hand targets at 10 Hz. During deployment, 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight runs on a single
NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU in synchronous closed-loop execution, streaming complete
30-step action chunks at 10 Hz while the SONIC decoder tracks each token in a
50 Hz balance and whole-body control loop.

blocks.en: Appendix G Discussion of Related Predictive Robot Policies
blocks.zh: 附录G 关于相关预测机器人政策的讨论

blocks.en:
While recent robotic policies increasingly incorporate future visual signals
beyond pixel reconstruction, they differ fundamentally in how future states are
represented and coupled to action generation. Implicit world-modeling methods
such as FLARE ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) (adopted in GR00T N1.5 ( NVIDIA, 2025 ) ) align
intermediate activations of an action diffusion transformer toward compact
action-aware embeddings via cosine loss. This shapes internal representations
during training without constructing an explicit spatial future stream that
participates in action denoising. Conversely, video-based WAMs ( Ye et al., 2026 ; Bi et al., 2026 ; Yuan et al., 2026 ) and codec-based unified policies such as F1 ( Lv et al., 2025 ) and InternVLA-A1 ( Cai et al., 2026a ) generate discrete tokens or continuous
latents of a separate pre-trained image or video tokenizer. Even when explicit
pixel decoding is omitted along the action path at test time, future generation
operates in a separate generative codec space rather than the visual
representation space that grounds VLM perception.

blocks.en:
Among policies that explicitly predict latent visual features, existing designs
rely on frozen target encoders. DreamVLA ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) supervises world
queries with dynamic regions, depth, and semantic features from frozen external
teachers and omits its prediction decoders at deployment, while
VLA-JEPA ( Sun et al., 2026 ) predicts latent states against a frozen external
V-JEPA 2 video encoder.
Closer in architecture is UniJEPA ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) , which also attaches a
feature-prediction expert and an action expert to a PaliGemma VLM in a
mixture-of-transformers, yet differs from 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight across target space,
prediction objective, and action coupling. First, UniJEPA predicts future features in the space of a frozen target encoder
(an initial SigLIP copy or DINOv3), while fine-tuning the policy’s own vision
encoder on robot data. Its action expert therefore reads current observations
and predicted futures from two different spaces that drift apart during
training. Second, its predictor uses deterministic MSE regression, collapsing
multimodal futures toward their conditional mean rather than modeling their
distribution. Third, its noise-free foresight stream is computed once in a
prefix pass and cached prior to action
denoising. 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -sight differs on all three axes: an online EMA of the policy’s own
causal video encoder keeps current observations and predicted futures in one
co-evolving feature space, foresight tokens are generated via conditional flow
matching, and foresight and continuous actions are denoised jointly across
shared Euler steps.
